evidence.activity: Op-Med: members submit long-form articles that Doximity publishes on its platform
evidence.quote: Members can submit Op-Med articles for publication on Doximity. These articles are long-form content written by clinicians for clinicians, covering topics such as front-line experiences and practice-changing viewpoints.
evidence.section: Item 1 > Our Tools for Medical Professionals > Newsfeed

creativity.criterion: level 2: specific current activity publishing clinicians' own written work, no reach figures disclosed

evidence.activity: Newsfeed clinical discussions where members discuss studies with peers and authors for peer-to-peer learning
evidence.quote: For example, members might discuss the results of a new clinical study, or even ask questions of the study’s author. Ultimately, this dialogue and interactivity drive engagement within the ecosystem and facilitate peer-to-peer education.
evidence.section: Item 1 > Our Tools for Medical Professionals > Newsfeed

community.criterion: level 2: specific current peer-to-peer education feature for non-employees, reach not quantified in the paragraph

evidence.activity: Residency Navigator, a free tool for medical students to research and compare residency programs
evidence.quote: Members beginning their medical careers can discover and compare training programs across the country using Residency Navigator, a tool that provides a transparent look into U.S. medical residency programs.
evidence.section: Item 1 > Our Tools for Medical Professionals > Professional Network > Careers
evidence.indicators: Approximately 90% of graduating U.S. medical students

community.criterion: level 2: specific current career-guidance tool for students outside the company; an information tool rather than a teaching program

evidence.activity: Dialer telehealth calls let clinicians add interpreters for patients
evidence.quote: Calls may be voice or video-based and include features such as customizable caller ID, the ability to add interpreters or additional participants, and seamless call handoffs across care teams.
evidence.section: Item 1 > Our Tools for Medical Professionals > Workflow Tools

cross_cultural.criterion: level 2: specific current language-access feature, limited and unquantified reach

creativity.reason: Level 2: Op-Med is a specific current feature that publishes clinicians' own long-form writing, with no scale indicators; other newsfeed and sponsored content is general web or marketing content and does not count.

community.reason: Level 2: specific current external-education features (peer-to-peer clinical discussion and the Residency Navigator tool for students) of limited or ambiguous educational depth, so the lower level is chosen over 3.

cross_cultural.reason: Level 2: a specific current customer-access feature (adding interpreters to telehealth calls) with no reach figures; the diversity-and-inclusion statement alone is general language.

entrepreneurship.reason: Level 0: the business description is detailed and shows no small-business customers and no enabling program; references to the company's own innovation are a trap term and are not enabling activity.

ai.notes: The human capital section is roughly 190 words, so coverage is sufficient. It contains only a general statement that the company 'prioritize[s] diversity and inclusion' and tracks unnamed metrics, which scores at most 1 and is superseded by E4. Excluded as traps: 'medical community' (network-effects language), Marketing Solutions that 'educate medical professionals about their brands' (marketing), 'physician training' (refers to competitor implementations), 'collaboration' with U.S. News & World Report (a commercial partnership), and 'innovate on our platform' (own innovation). E3 is borderline for Community because it is a career-information tool rather than education. It has a strong reach indicator (about 90% of graduating U.S. medical students), but it was kept at level 2 per the 'when torn, pick lower' rule. The platform reaches over 3 million registered members, but that figure is not in the same paragraph as the newsfeed education quote, so it is not used as an indicator. Op-Med for Creativity is also borderline (clinical opinion writing versus creative work) and was scored at the minimum qualifying level. The Item 7 excerpts repeat the Item 1 overview and add no new activities.
